title: Alpine Ski House
sections:
Alpine Ski House operates four ski resorts and a central office in Denver. The company has 1,200 year-round employees and hires about 2,000 seasonal employees every winter. Seasonal employees use shared kiosks in the rental shops and sign in with their own accounts.

The company started a program to use AI agents for guest services, lift operations and ticketing. The program is in a pilot phase that will last until the end of the ski season.

**Identity and licensing**

Alpine Ski House has a Microsoft 365 tenant that uses Microsoft Entra ID. All year-round employees have Microsoft 365 E5 licenses, 400 employees have Microsoft 365 Copilot licenses, and the tenant has Microsoft Agent 365 licenses. Seasonal employees have Microsoft 365 F3 licenses.

The tenant contains the following groups:

- AgentPilot: a security group that contains every user who takes part in the agent pilot
- GuestServicesManagers: the managers of the guest services teams
- MountainOps: the mountain operations staff
- LiftOperators: the lift operators, all of whom are also members of MountainOps

MountainOps and LiftOperators are members of AgentPilot.

User5 is the IT governance lead. User5 is not a sponsor of any agent.

**Agents**

- Lift Status: a custom agent built in Microsoft Copilot Studio by the mountain operations developers. It is published to the organization. Last week, a developer published an update to the agent.
- Trail Guide: an agent built by a guest services manager in Microsoft Copilot Agent Builder. The manager submitted the agent for admin approval.
- Ski Rental Partner: an agent built by an external partner that offers equipment rental bookings.
- Several Microsoft Entra agent identities were created for agents that ran during last season's events. Some of them no longer have a sponsor because the sponsors left the company.

**Tools**

The ticketing team operates an internal remote MCP server named TicketingMCP that has a publicly accessible endpoint and uses API key authentication. A developer registered TicketingMCP with Agent 365 by using the Agent 365 CLI. An AI Administrator approved the request and granted consent.

- During the pilot, only pilot participants must be able to use agents and plugins.
- Agents and plugins from external publishers must not be installable by any user.
- Only guest services managers may share Agent Builder agents broadly with others in the organization.
- Users must keep using the current version of Lift Status until an administrator reviews the latest update.
- Trail Guide must be installable only by the members of MountainOps after an administrator approves it.
- Lift Status must be installable by all MountainOps members. Lift operators must have Lift Status installed for them without any action and must see it pinned in Microsoft 365 Copilot.

- Agent identities for which no tokens were issued during the last 60 days must be disabled automatically. Agent identities must never be deleted automatically.
- Sponsors must be notified before an inactive agent identity is disabled. If an agent identity has no sponsor or owner, User5 must be notified instead.
- The ticketing team will build a low-code agent that uses TicketingMCP. The agent must invoke TicketingMCP through the approved registration so that the security team can monitor tool invocations.
- Use the Microsoft 365 admin center for agent governance wherever possible, and minimize custom scripting.

- The help desk must be able to handle all agent-related tickets during peak season, so changes must be made before December 1.
- The kiosks in the rental shops are shared devices and must not receive new software during the season.
- Administrators must use the least privileged role for each task.
